text:
maria.g: Quick q — trying to capture a ~30s inference trace for a Llama2-13B run to generate a flamegraph. The raw trace is huge (~28GB). What's the recommended flow: nsys -> chrome trace, or torch.profiler for op-level flamegraphs? Any preferred sanitization steps before sharing? Need to hand off to perf team.

sam: For system+CUDA timeline use nsys -> export to chrome/perfetto. torch.profiler is useful for op-level breakdowns but it can blow up if you record shapes/inputs. My usual flow is a short reprex (seq_len=128, batch=1) and capture both: nsys for host/CUDA timeline + torch.profiler for op detail.

jun: Agreed. For nsys I often do something like:
```
nsys profile -o trace/session1 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=none --stop-after 60s python run_infer.py --seq 128
```
That helps keep the qdrep sized down. Then export chrome trace:
```
nsys export trace/session1.qdrep -o session1_chrome.json --format=json
```
(we usually trim down the capture time and warm up before starting).

eva: Two quick tips: 1) do a couple warmup inferences so KV cache/warmup doesn't dominate the flamegraph; run capture after warmup. 2) redact any prompt/user text before sharing. We have a tiny scrub step, e.g.:
```
sed -E 's/\"input_text\": \"[^\"]+\"/\"input_text\": \"<REDACTED>\"/g' session1_chrome.json > session1_redacted.json
```
Works well for the chrome trace JSON.

sam: :thumbsup: And if you need op-level flamegraphs, torch.profiler is good:
```
with torch.profiler.profile(use_cuda=True, record_shapes=True, profile_memory=True) as p:
    model(input)
# then p.export_chrome_trace('torch_trace.json')
```
If size explodes, set record_shapes=False and avoid profile_memory.

maria.g: Perfect — I'll do a short nsys capture + a torch.profiler run. One logistical Q: where should I upload redacted traces for the perf team to pick up?

infra-bot: maria.g: Created presigned S3 upload: https://upload.internal.redwood/s/xyz123 (expires in 72h). Please upload under perf-uploads/eng-runtime/maria/ and include a README with the capture commandline, CUDA/driver/pytorch versions, and model revision.

jun: When you upload, also add the nsys version (`nsys --version`) and a one-liner showing how you invoked the workload (env + cmd). That saves a lot of back-and-forth.

maria.g: Running captures now (shorter seq + warmups). I'll redact and upload to that link then post the README. Thanks all :raised_hands:

sam: :eyes: ping me when uploaded — I'll do a quick sanity check for obvious regressions (long kernel stacks, unexpected memcpy spikes).
